Raycast launched a new feature called "Screen Awareness" that lets users bring the content of the app or window they are currently using directly into AI Chat. Here is a detailed introduction.

Raycast AI can now read what's on your screen

When using AI chatbots like ChatGPT, Claude or Raycast AI, many people often have to keep copying and pasting text, uploading screenshots, or explaining what they're working on before they can ask AI for help.

Raycast recently updated a feature hoping to simplify this workflow, letting Raycast AI access the contents of the currently focused window directly.

Raycast said this feature, called "Screen Awareness," can "bring the content of the app or window you have focused into AI Chat or Quick AI, so you don't have to copy text, attach screenshots, or explain what you're looking at."

Use the "Send Focused Window to AI" command, pick Screen Awareness from the @ menu, or simply say "summarise this" or "reply to this."

Once activated, what's sent to Raycast AI can include detailed information about the app and window, selected text, focused controls, and a screenshot of the focused window.

On Mac, if triggered from Finder, it can also provide information about selected files or folders; while Raycast's Browser Companion can capture web page details and content beyond the visible screen.

According to the company, users can set up a shortcut to activate Screen Awareness through a brief tutorial that appears the first time they use the command. Raycast said their team "loves double-tapping the right Command key." Users can also set keyboard shortcuts for related commands, such as Send Selected Text to AI, Send Screen Area to AI, and Send Screen to AI.

Here are all the new features included in Raycast v0.71:

AI: The Send Focused Window to AI command now includes richer app and window content information AI: Added the Ask Screen Awareness AI Extension for quickly feeding content to Raycast AI AI: Added compression and content management support Quick AI: The "Send Message" AI settings now also apply to Quick AI, letting you submit queries with Command Return Dictation: Added ways to import vocabulary and shortcuts from other apps Dictation: Added an "Add Word to Vocabulary" command to add selected words or typed parameters to your vocabulary Feedback: Added the Ask Feedback AI Extension for contacting the Raycast team Hotkeys: Support for simultaneous modifier key combinations on both sides of the keyboard (e.g. Left ⌘ + Right ⌘), which can be recorded and displayed in the Hotkey Recorder
